1.description: Early snowdrop shoots appearing in sheltered spots, Ireland's mild Gulf Stream climate brings them out sooner than much of Britain
1.childFriendlyNote: Tiny white bells are already pushing up through the cold ground. Ireland is so mild they come early!

1.description: Robins singing loudly from bare branches, defending winter territories with their bright red breast puffed out
1.childFriendlyNote: A little bird with a bright red tummy sits on a branch and sings its heart out, even in the cold!

1.description: Fox mating season. Eerie barking screams echo through the night in both countryside and city
1.childFriendlyNote: Listen after dark for a spooky scream. That's a fox calling to its friends in the night!

1.description: Flocks of fieldfares feeding on hawthorn berries in hedgerows, winter visitors from Scandinavia
1.childFriendlyNote: Big flocks of speckled birds chatter as they gobble up red berries from the hedges

1.description: Gorse bushes showing scattered yellow flowers even in midwinter, their coconut scent faint in cold air
1.childFriendlyNote: Even in winter, prickly gorse bushes have bright yellow flowers. Lean in carefully and sniff for coconut!

1.description: Jelly ear fungus growing on dead elder branches, brown and rubbery in the damp Irish winter
1.childFriendlyNote: Wobbly brown ears growing on branches. Jelly ear fungus feels just like a cold, rubbery ear!

2.description: Snowdrop patches spreading in churchyards and old gardens, white bells nodding in the breeze
2.childFriendlyNote: More little white lanterns are popping up every day, nodding hello in the wind

2.description: Long yellow catkins dangling from bare hazel branches, releasing clouds of pollen on dry days
2.childFriendlyNote: Fuzzy yellow tails hang from branches like caterpillars. Shake one gently and watch golden dust fly

2.description: Robins singing at dawn and dusk, one of the only birds in full voice during the dark months
2.childFriendlyNote: The robin sings even when it's dark and cold. It's one of the bravest little singers in Ireland!

2.description: Rooks returning to rookeries in tall trees, noisy groups cawing and refurbishing stick nests
2.childFriendlyNote: Big black birds with pale beaks are gathering in the treetops, shouting and fixing their twiggy homes

2.description: Gorse bushes beginning to show more yellow flowers on mild coastal hillsides
2.childFriendlyNote: The prickly gorse is waking up, more yellow flowers every week, smelling like sweet coconut

3.description: Snowdrops in full flower, carpeting woodland edges and old estate grounds across Ireland
3.childFriendlyNote: The ground is covered in little white bells, like a fairy village stretching through the trees

3.description: Hazel catkins at their longest, swinging in the wind and dusting everything with yellow pollen
3.childFriendlyNote: The fuzzy yellow tails are at their longest now. They swing and bounce in the wind

3.description: Fox mating calls still heard at night, vixens seeking den sites for coming cubs
3.childFriendlyNote: The foxes are still screaming at night. The mum fox is looking for a cosy den for her babies

3.description: Rookeries getting noisier, birds stealing sticks from each other's nests in tall beeches and ashes
3.childFriendlyNote: The rooks are building nests and arguing. They steal sticks from each other when nobody's looking!

3.description: Gorse flowering increasing on hillsides and coastal paths, bright yellow against grey winter landscape
3.childFriendlyNote: More golden flowers on the prickly gorse. They're like little suns dotted across the hillside

3.description: Fieldfares still in hedgerows and fields, chattering flocks working through last berries
3.childFriendlyNote: The visiting birds from the north are still here, chattering as they hunt for berries

4.description: Snowdrops at peak, dense white drifts in sheltered spots, some early flowers beginning to fade
4.childFriendlyNote: Snowdrops everywhere! So many white bells the ground looks like it snowed

4.description: Hazel catkins shedding pollen freely, tiny red female flowers visible on the same branches if you look closely
4.childFriendlyNote: Look really closely at the hazel branch. Can you spot the tiny red flowers? They're smaller than a ladybird!

4.description: Dunnocks starting to sing from hedgerow tops, a rapid sweet warble often overlooked
4.childFriendlyNote: A shy brown bird hops along the hedge bottom then suddenly sings a fast happy tune from the top!

4.description: Rooks actively building nests, flying back and forth with sticks, rookeries at full volume
4.childFriendlyNote: The rooks are so busy! Watch them fly to and fro with sticks. Their treetop village is getting noisy

4.description: Gorse flowering building on hillsides and coastal cliffs, coconut scent stronger on warm days
4.childFriendlyNote: More and more yellow gorse. If the sun warms the flowers, close your eyes and sniff for coconut

4.description: First frogs stirring in mild parts of Ireland, moving towards breeding ponds on damp nights
4.childFriendlyNote: Frogs are waking up from their winter sleep and hopping towards the nearest pond in the dark!

5.description: Snowdrops still strong but earliest flowers starting to turn papery at the edges
5.childFriendlyNote: The first snowdrops are getting tired. Their petals are going soft and see-through

5.description: First lesser celandine leaves appearing along hedge banks and damp woodland edges
5.childFriendlyNote: Shiny heart-shaped leaves are poking up along the paths. Their yellow star-flowers will come soon

5.description: Frogs gathering at breeding ponds, males calling with low purring croaks in the evening
5.childFriendlyNote: Listen near the pond at dusk. The frogs are purring like tiny motorbikes as they call for a mate

5.description: Purple, yellow and white crocuses opening in parks, gardens and churchyards across Irish towns
5.childFriendlyNote: Purple, yellow and white cups pop open in the grass. They close up tight when it gets cold again

5.description: Dunnocks in full song from hedge tops, pairs chasing each other in quick fluttery flights
5.childFriendlyNote: The shy brown bird sings its fast happy song from the tippy-top of the hedge every morning now

6.description: Snowdrops fading, seed pods swelling as flowers collapse, last blooms in shaded spots
6.childFriendlyNote: The snowdrops are drooping and going green. They're making seeds now, ready for next year

6.description: Lesser celandine flowers opening, glossy yellow stars on hedge banks and woodland edges
6.childFriendlyNote: Shiny yellow star-flowers are opening along the paths. They close up on cloudy days

6.description: Frogs spawning in garden ponds, ditches and bog pools: clumps of jelly appearing in still water
6.childFriendlyNote: Blobs of see-through jelly with tiny black dots in the pond. Each dot will become a baby frog!

6.description: Crocuses at peak in parks and gardens, bees visiting the open cups on sunny mornings
6.childFriendlyNote: The colourful crocus cups are wide open and bees are diving in headfirst for a drink of nectar!

6.description: First primroses opening on sheltered banks in the mild southwest, pale yellow flowers close to the ground
6.childFriendlyNote: Soft yellow flowers peep out from the bottom of the hedgerow. Primroses mean spring is really coming!

6.description: Gorse flowering strongly now, hillsides and roadside banks turning yellow, sweet coconut scent carrying
6.childFriendlyNote: The hillsides are going golden! The prickly gorse smells like coconut ice cream on a warm day

7.description: Celandine spreading along hedge banks and stream sides, glossy leaves and bright yellow flowers
7.childFriendlyNote: Yellow stars twinkle all along the path. They open in the sunshine and hide on cloudy days

7.description: Frogspawn everywhere in ponds and ditches, swelling clumps of jelly with black embryos visible
7.childFriendlyNote: The frogspawn blobs are getting bigger. You can see the tiny black tadpoles wriggling inside!

7.description: Primroses appearing on hedge banks and woodland edges across the south and west
7.childFriendlyNote: Pale yellow primroses are popping up everywhere along the hedge. Spring is really here!

7.description: Gorse at full flower on hills and coast, coconut scent strong on warm days, pods beginning to form on earliest flowers
7.childFriendlyNote: The gorse is blazing yellow! Stand near it on a sunny day and breathe in the sweet coconut smell

7.description: Song thrush singing from rooftops and tree tops at dusk, repeating each phrase two or three times
7.childFriendlyNote: A brown bird on the rooftop sings the same tune twice, then a new one. It's like a DJ mixing songs!

7.description: Rooks incubating eggs in their treetop rookeries, one bird sits tight while the other brings food
7.childFriendlyNote: The rooks are sitting on their eggs now. One stays on the nest while the other goes shopping for food!

8.description: Primroses spreading along hedgerows and woodland rides, pale yellow flowers clustered on hairy stems
8.childFriendlyNote: Primroses everywhere! Their soft yellow flowers have a sweet gentle smell if you get close

8.description: Celandine carpeting damp woodland floors and stream banks, flowers closing on overcast days
8.childFriendlyNote: The woodland floor sparkles with yellow stars, but they shut tight when the clouds come!

8.description: Frogspawn swelling, embryos developing into comma shapes, some early spawn hatching into tadpoles
8.childFriendlyNote: The little black dots in the jelly are growing wiggly tails. They're turning into tadpoles!

8.description: Gorse at peak flower, entire hillsides blazing yellow, the saying goes 'when gorse is out of bloom, kissing is out of fashion'
8.childFriendlyNote: The hills are painted golden yellow with gorse! There's an old saying that gorse is never out of flower

8.description: Song thrush in full voice from treetops and aerials, each phrase repeated like a musical conversation
8.childFriendlyNote: The song thrush sings the same little tune twice or three times. Can you count how many times it repeats?

8.description: Wild and garden daffodils beginning to bloom, golden trumpets appearing in parks and roadsides
8.childFriendlyNote: Golden trumpets are popping up in gardens and parks. The daffodils are here!

9.description: Primroses at peak across Ireland, lining every country lane and hedge bank
9.childFriendlyNote: Every hedge bank is dotted with soft yellow primroses: Ireland's favourite spring flower!

9.description: Daffodils in full bloom across parks, gardens and roadsides, brightening up the late-winter landscape
9.childFriendlyNote: Daffodils are dancing everywhere. Their golden trumpets bob and nod in the March breeze

9.description: Tadpoles hatching from frogspawn, tiny black wrigglers clinging to empty jelly in ponds
9.childFriendlyNote: The baby tadpoles have hatched! Tiny black wrigglers cling to the leftover jelly like little commas

9.description: First blackthorn blossom appearing on bare thorny hedgerow branches, white flowers before leaves
9.childFriendlyNote: The dark spiky hedge suddenly has white flowers, like popcorn stuck on bare black branches!

9.description: Gorse still blazing yellow, early pods beginning to form as flowers fade on sun-facing slopes
9.childFriendlyNote: The gorse is still glowing golden on the hills. On a hot day you might hear the seed pods pop!

9.description: Pussy willow catkins soft and silvery on goat willow branches, turning golden with pollen
9.childFriendlyNote: Soft silvery puffs on the willow branches feel like tiny kittens' paws. That's why they're called pussy willows!

10.description: Primroses at peak, covering hedge banks and woodland floors across Ireland, a true emblem of Irish spring
10.childFriendlyNote: Primroses are everywhere. Every bank and ditch is dotted with soft yellow flowers

10.description: Blackthorn hedgerows turning white with blossom, flowers appearing before any leaves emerge
10.childFriendlyNote: The hedgerows are covered in white flowers on dark branches. It looks like they're wearing snowflake coats!

10.description: Tadpoles growing in ponds, swimming in shoals near the surface on warm days
10.childFriendlyNote: Wiggly tadpoles swim together in a big group near the top of the pond to catch the warm sunshine

10.description: First chiffchaffs arriving from Africa, singing their two-note name from willow and birch tops
10.childFriendlyNote: This tiny bird flew all the way from Africa and sings its own name: "chiff-chaff, chiff-chaff"!

10.description: Queen bumblebees emerging from hibernation, visiting willow catkins and early garden flowers
10.childFriendlyNote: A big fuzzy bee bumbles past. She's a queen looking for a cosy hole to build her home in!

10.description: Pussy willow catkins turning golden yellow with pollen, buzzing with bees on sunny mornings
10.childFriendlyNote: The soft silvery puffs have turned golden and are covered in happy buzzing bees having breakfast!

11.description: Primroses still glorious across hedgerows and woodland, this is peak Irish primrose season
11.childFriendlyNote: Still so many primroses! They smile up from the hedge bank like little yellow faces

11.description: Blackthorn in full bloom, white blossom clouds along every hedgerow, sometimes called the 'blackthorn winter' cold snap
11.childFriendlyNote: White flowers cover the dark thorny hedge like a cloud. People say a cold snap comes when the blackthorn blooms!

11.description: Chiffchaffs now widespread, their repetitive two-note song one of the first spring sounds in every woodland
11.childFriendlyNote: "Chiff-chaff, chiff-chaff". Can you hear it? This little bird never gets tired of saying its name!

11.description: Daffodils at peak in parks, gardens and along roadsides, golden and white varieties shining
11.childFriendlyNote: Fields of golden daffodils are bobbing in the breeze like they're all waving hello!

11.description: Bumblebee queens actively nest-hunting, buzzing low over the ground searching for mouse holes
11.childFriendlyNote: Watch the big furry bee flying low along the ground. She's house-hunting for the perfect hole!

11.description: Wood sorrel unfolding trefoil leaves on woodland floors, one candidate for the original Irish shamrock
11.childFriendlyNote: Three little heart-shaped leaves fold up like tiny umbrellas. Some people think this is the real shamrock!

12.description: Primroses still blooming strongly, though earliest flowers starting to set seed
12.childFriendlyNote: The primroses are still going strong. Ireland's hedgerows are lined with pale yellow

12.description: Blackthorn blossom beginning to fade, first tiny green leaves unfurling on thorny branches
12.childFriendlyNote: The white blackthorn flowers are falling like snow and little green leaves are starting to grow instead

12.description: Chiffchaffs singing from every woodland and garden, establishing territories for nesting
12.childFriendlyNote: The chiffchaffs are singing so loud now. Each one has picked its favourite tree to sing from!

12.description: Wood sorrel flowering in old woodlands, delicate white petals veined with pink above shamrock-like leaves
12.childFriendlyNote: Tiny white flowers with pink stripes sit above three-leaf clovers. This might be the real shamrock of St Patrick!

12.description: Tadpoles growing fast in warming ponds, developing external gills, feeding on algae
12.childFriendlyNote: The tadpoles are getting bigger! They munch on green slimy algae and swim in wiggly circles

12.description: Gorse still flowering strongly, seed pods starting to form on lower branches, bees buzzing around blooms
12.childFriendlyNote: The golden gorse is humming with bees. On a hot day the black seed pods go pop like tiny fireworks!

13.description: Primroses beginning to fade, flowers going papery as bluebells start to take over woodland floors
13.childFriendlyNote: The primroses are getting tired now, but look, bluebells are coming to take their place!

13.description: First swallows arriving from Africa, skimming low over fields and water, a sign that summer is coming
13.childFriendlyNote: The swallows are back from Africa! Watch them swoop low over the fields catching tiny flying bugs

13.description: Blackthorn blossom fading, green leaves replacing white flowers, small fruitlets beginning to form
13.childFriendlyNote: The white blackthorn flowers are gone and green leaves are covering the hedge. Summer clothes are going on!

13.description: First orange-tip butterflies on the wing, males with bright orange wing tips patrolling hedgerows
13.childFriendlyNote: A white butterfly with bright orange wing tips flutters along the hedge. Only the boys have the orange!

13.description: Wild garlic leaves carpeting damp woodland floors, the strong garlicky smell hitting you before you see them
13.childFriendlyNote: Walk into the woods and sniff. Can you smell garlic? Look down and you'll see a carpet of green leaves!

13.description: Chiffchaffs nesting now, still singing loudly from canopy to mark territory
13.childFriendlyNote: "Chiff-chaff, chiff-chaff". The little bird is still singing away while its partner builds a nest in the bushes

14.description: More swallows arriving daily, swooping over farmyards and fields, long forked tails flashing
14.childFriendlyNote: More swallows are arriving every day. Watch their long tail feathers stream behind them like ribbons!

14.description: Wild garlic spreading fast through damp woodlands, leaves broadening, first flower buds forming
14.childFriendlyNote: The garlic smell in the woods is getting stronger! Soon the green carpet will be covered in white star flowers

14.description: Orange-tip butterflies increasing along hedgerows, females laying eggs on cuckoo flower stems
14.childFriendlyNote: The orange-tipped butterflies are everywhere now. Can you spot one landing on a pink cuckoo flower?

14.description: Gorse approaching peak spring flowering, hillsides ablaze with yellow, seed pods cracking in the sunshine
14.childFriendlyNote: The hills are blazing yellow! Listen closely on a hot day. You might hear the gorse pods popping!

14.description: First bluebell shoots pushing through woodland leaf litter, green spears with flower buds tightly furled
14.childFriendlyNote: Green spears are pushing through the brown leaves on the forest floor. The bluebells are coming!

14.description: Cuckoo flower (lady's smock) blooming in damp meadows and along ditches, pale pink petals
14.childFriendlyNote: Pale pink flowers on thin stems sway in wet meadows. They bloom when the cuckoo is supposed to arrive!

15.description: Bluebells starting to open in sheltered woodlands, first hints of the blue haze to come
15.childFriendlyNote: The first bluebells are opening! Their sweet smell fills the wood like a gentle perfume

15.description: Swallows now widespread, settling into barns and outbuildings, beginning to build mud cup nests
15.childFriendlyNote: The swallows are making mud cups on barn walls. They carry tiny beakfuls of mud from puddles!

15.description: Wild garlic in full flower, white star-shaped blooms above broad green leaves, pungent scent fills the woods
15.childFriendlyNote: The woods are full of white flowers and the garlic smell is so strong. You can smell it from the path!

15.description: First cuckoos calling across bogs and farmland, the male's loud "cuck-oo" carrying far on still mornings
15.childFriendlyNote: "Cuck-oo! Cuck-oo!". This sneaky bird lays its eggs in other birds' nests so they do all the hard work!

15.description: Hawthorn hedges greening up fast, bright green leaf clusters bursting from thorny branches
15.childFriendlyNote: The hedges are turning green! Tiny bright leaves are bursting out of every branch like green fireworks

15.description: Orange-tips at peak along hedgerows and country lanes, a classic Irish spring butterfly
15.childFriendlyNote: Orange-tips are fluttering everywhere! When they close their wings they look like little green leaves

16.description: Bluebells spreading across ancient woodland floors, a shimmering blue-purple carpet under the trees
16.childFriendlyNote: The woods have turned blue! A magical carpet of bluebells stretches between the trees

16.description: Swallows swooping low over fields and water, chattering from wires and barn roofs
16.childFriendlyNote: Swallows sit on the wires chattering to each other, then zoom off to catch flies, so fast!

16.description: Cuckoo calling from woodland edges and over bogs, females scouting for nests of meadow pipits and dunnocks
16.childFriendlyNote: "Cuck-oo!" echoes across the fields. The sneaky lady cuckoo is looking for another bird's nest to use!

16.description: Wild garlic at peak flower, woodland floors white and pungent, bees visiting the star-shaped blooms
16.childFriendlyNote: The whole wood smells like a pizza restaurant! White star flowers and that amazing garlic pong

16.description: Hawthorn hedges fully leafed out, first flower buds forming in clusters, the 'May blossom' nearly ready
16.childFriendlyNote: The hedges are thick with green leaves now and little bundles of flower buds are getting ready to pop

16.description: Cow parsley shooting up along lanes and hedge bases, feathery green leaves and white flower heads starting
16.childFriendlyNote: Tall feathery plants are growing fast along every lane. Their white flower heads look like tiny umbrellas

17.description: Bluebells at peak, ancient woodlands filled with sweet scent and shimmering blue-purple haze
17.childFriendlyNote: The bluebell woods are absolutely magical right now. Close your eyes and breathe in the sweet perfume

17.description: First hawthorn flowers opening, creamy white blossom with a musky sweet scent, the 'May' is nearly here
17.childFriendlyNote: The hawthorn is starting to bloom! In Ireland people say the fairy trees are putting on their dresses

17.description: Cow parsley frothing along every lane and hedgerow, white flower heads creating a lacy border
17.childFriendlyNote: Every country lane has a frothy white border of cow parsley. It looks like someone sprayed the hedges with foam!

17.description: Cuckoo at peak calling period, the sound carrying across bogs, farmland and woodland edges
17.childFriendlyNote: "Cuck-oo! Cuck-oo!". It's the loudest time for cuckoos, you can hear them from far away!

17.description: First swifts arriving, screaming in groups over towns and villages, these birds almost never land
17.childFriendlyNote: Look up! Screaming dark birds zoom over the rooftops. Swifts eat, sleep and even drink while flying!

17.description: Foxglove rosettes growing tall along banks and woodland edges, flower spikes beginning to form
17.childFriendlyNote: Tall fuzzy stems are shooting up along the lane. Soon they'll be covered in spotty purple bells

18.description: Bluebells still stunning but earliest flowers starting to droop and lose colour
18.childFriendlyNote: The bluebells are still beautiful but the oldest ones are going floppy. Enjoy them while they last!

18.description: Hawthorn hedges bursting into white blossom, the May blossom filling lanes with its sweet musky scent
18.childFriendlyNote: The hawthorn hedges are covered in white flowers! In Ireland these are fairy trees. Never cut one down!

18.description: Swifts now screaming over Irish towns in the evenings, dark scythe-shaped silhouettes against the sky
18.childFriendlyNote: The swifts are screaming around the rooftops! They look like little dark boomerangs zooming through the sky

18.description: Cow parsley at peak, roadsides and lanes a mass of white lacy flower heads above feathery leaves
18.childFriendlyNote: Roadsides are like a white wedding! Cow parsley everywhere, tall and frothy and beautiful

18.description: Puffins arriving at breeding colonies on Skellig Michael, Saltee Islands and Rathlin Island, colourful beaks bright
18.childFriendlyNote: The puffins are back on the islands! They look like tiny clowns with their bright orange beaks

18.description: Foxglove spikes getting taller, first purple bell flowers opening at the bottom of the spike
18.childFriendlyNote: The foxglove is opening its purple bells from the bottom up. Bees crawl right inside them!

19.description: Hawthorn at peak blossom, hedgerows a mass of creamy white flowers buzzing with insects
19.childFriendlyNote: Every hedge is covered in white May blossom. Lean close and hear it humming with hundreds of bees!

19.description: Swifts screaming over rooftops in the long evenings, parties of birds chasing each other at high speed
19.childFriendlyNote: Wild screaming parties of swifts race around the rooftops. They sleep on the wing, flying all night!

19.description: Foxgloves opening along woodland edges, banks and lanes, purple spotted bells climbing the tall spikes
19.childFriendlyNote: Tall purple foxgloves are like fairy towers. Peek inside a bell and see the spotty pattern!

19.description: Puffins busy on island colonies, digging burrows and courting, bills brightly coloured for breeding
19.childFriendlyNote: The puffins are digging burrows on the cliffs to lay their eggs. They use their feet like shovels!

19.description: Cow parsley still frothing along lanes, beginning to go over, seed heads forming
19.childFriendlyNote: The white cow parsley is starting to droop and go brown. It's making seeds for next year

19.description: First damselflies appearing over ponds and streams, electric blue bodies flickering over the water
19.childFriendlyNote: Tiny blue helicopters hover over the pond. They're damselflies and they can fly backwards!

20.description: Hawthorn blossom still going strong, petals beginning to fall like confetti on breezy days
20.childFriendlyNote: Walk under the hawthorn and white petals fall like snow. Catch one in your hand!

20.description: Foxgloves at peak, tall purple spikes lining woodland edges and roadside banks
20.childFriendlyNote: The foxgloves are the tallest now. Look at the spotty insides of each purple bell, like a secret map!

20.description: Swifts at peak, screaming parties over towns in warm evenings, nesting under eaves and in old walls
20.childFriendlyNote: The swifts are zooming and screaming overhead. They fly about 500 miles every single day!

20.description: Puffins incubating eggs in burrows on Skellig Michael and Saltee Islands, taking turns sitting
20.childFriendlyNote: The puffins are keeping their single egg warm deep in a burrow. Mum and dad take turns!

20.description: Buttercups opening in meadows and grasslands, golden yellow flowers shining in the sunshine
20.childFriendlyNote: Hold a buttercup under your chin. If it glows yellow, you like butter! (Everyone does!)

20.description: Damselflies more common now, pairs flying in tandem over ponds, brilliant blue bodies catching the light
20.childFriendlyNote: Blue damselflies fly stuck together making a heart shape with their bodies, how romantic!

21.description: Foxgloves at peak, tall purple spikes standing like sentinels along every bank and woodland edge
21.childFriendlyNote: The foxgloves are the stars of the show! Fat bumblebees crawl deep inside the spotted purple bells

21.description: Buttercups at peak, meadows and playing fields glowing golden yellow
21.childFriendlyNote: The fields are golden with buttercups! Pick one and hold it under your friend's chin

21.description: Hawthorn blossom fading, petals falling and small green berries beginning to form
21.childFriendlyNote: The hawthorn flowers are turning into tiny green berries. They'll go red by autumn!

21.description: Puffins incubating on island colonies, standing guard at burrow entrances, preening colourful beaks
21.childFriendlyNote: Puffins stand at the door of their burrows looking out to sea like little clown-faced doorkeepers!

21.description: Meadowsweet beginning to flower along streams and in damp meadows, frothy cream flower heads appearing
21.childFriendlyNote: Creamy frothy flowers are popping up along the stream. Crush a leaf and it smells like medicine!

21.description: Common spotted orchids appearing in meadows, roadsides and even lawns, pink-purple spotted flower spikes
21.childFriendlyNote: A real wild orchid growing in the grass! Look at the tiny spotted flowers. Each one is like a little face

22.description: Foxgloves still magnificent, lower flowers fading as upper bells continue to open
22.childFriendlyNote: The bottom foxglove bells are going floppy but new ones keep opening at the top like a tower growing upwards!

22.description: Meadowsweet blooming along every stream and ditch, sweet almond-honey scent on warm evenings
22.childFriendlyNote: Creamy frothy flowers along the stream smell like sweet honey and almonds. Breathe in deep!

22.description: Fuchsia hedges beginning to bloom in the west and southwest, magenta and purple flowers dangling like earrings
22.childFriendlyNote: The fuchsia hedges are growing little dangling pink and purple flowers. They look like fairy earrings!

22.description: Common blue butterflies appearing in grasslands and meadows, males a vivid blue, females brownish
22.childFriendlyNote: A tiny blue butterfly dances over the grass. It's smaller than your thumb but so bright blue!

22.description: Bog cotton dotting blanket bogs and wet hillsides, white fluffy heads bobbing in the breeze
22.childFriendlyNote: White fluffy balls bob on the bog like cotton wool stuck on sticks. They're softer than you'd think!

22.description: Puffin chicks hatching in burrows, parents beginning fishing trips to bring back sand eels
22.childFriendlyNote: Baby puffins are hatching in their dark burrows! Mum and dad bring them tiny fish to eat

23.description: Fuchsia hedges in full flower across Munster and the west coast, magenta flowers dripping from every branch
23.childFriendlyNote: The fuchsia hedges are covered in pink and purple dancers. Squeeze a bud gently and it pops open!

23.description: Meadowsweet at peak along streams, ditches and damp meadows, the scent intoxicating on still evenings
23.childFriendlyNote: The meadowsweet smells so good by the stream tonight. People used to scatter it on their floors as perfume!

23.description: Bog cotton at peak, blanket bogs appearing snow-covered with thousands of white fluffy seed heads
23.childFriendlyNote: The bog looks like it's snowing in summer! Thousands of white fluffy balls dance in the wind

23.description: Common blues widespread in grasslands and sand dunes, fluttering low over wildflowers
23.childFriendlyNote: Little blue jewels flutter over the flowers. When they close their wings, they show silvery spots underneath

23.description: Puffins busy feeding chicks, flying back with beaks crammed full of sand eels lined up neatly
23.childFriendlyNote: Puffins fly home with beaks full of little fish all lined up. How do they catch more without dropping the first ones?

23.description: Common spotted orchids at peak in meadows and roadsides, pink-purple spikes amid the grass
23.childFriendlyNote: Wild orchids in the grass! Each tiny flower has spots and stripes like a little butterfly mask

24.description: Fuchsia hedges spectacular in west Cork, Kerry and Connemara, magenta flowers glowing in the summer light
24.childFriendlyNote: The fuchsia hedges in the west of Ireland are dripping with pink and purple flowers. They're so pretty!

24.description: Meadowsweet lining every waterway, creamy flower heads billowing like foam, sweet scent everywhere
24.childFriendlyNote: Every stream and ditch is lined with creamy frothy flowers that smell like honey and marzipan

24.description: Bog cotton still beautiful on blanket bogs, fluffy heads starting to shed on windy days
24.childFriendlyNote: The bog cotton is starting to blow away. Catch a fluffy bit floating on the breeze!

24.description: Puffin chicks growing fast in burrows, parents making constant fishing trips from Skellig and Saltee colonies
24.childFriendlyNote: Baby puffins (called pufflings!) are getting big and fluffy in their dark burrows, eating fish all day

24.description: Foxgloves past peak, lower bells fallen, upper flowers still open, seed pods forming below
24.childFriendlyNote: The foxglove is making seeds now. Shake a dry pod gently and hundreds of tiny seeds fall out like dust!

24.description: Traditional hay meadows at peak colour with knapweed, clover, vetch and yellow rattle creating a tapestry
24.childFriendlyNote: The meadow is buzzing with bees and full of every colour: pink, purple, yellow, white! It's a flower party!

25.description: Fuchsia hedges at their most spectacular, a signature sight of the Irish summer west coast landscape
25.childFriendlyNote: Fuchsia flowers are the jewels of Irish hedges. Each dangling flower is like a tiny ballerina!

25.description: Meadowsweet still fragrant along waterways, earliest flower heads turning brown at the edges
25.childFriendlyNote: The meadowsweet is still smelling lovely but some flowers are going brown. Summer is halfway through!

25.description: Puffin chicks (pufflings) growing rapidly, parents still ferrying fish back to island burrows
25.childFriendlyNote: The pufflings are getting big. Soon they'll be ready to jump off the cliffs and swim for the first time!

25.description: Common blues at peak in meadows, coastal grasslands and sand dunes across Ireland
25.childFriendlyNote: So many tiny blue butterflies! They love clover flowers and dance around them all day

25.description: Hay meadows still colourful, grasses heavy with seed heads, insects buzzing and chirping
25.childFriendlyNote: Run your hand through the tall grass and feel the feathery seed heads tickle your fingers

25.description: Red clover blooming in meadows and field margins, fuzzy pink-purple flower heads visited by bumblebees
25.childFriendlyNote: Pull a tiny pink tube from the clover flower head and suck the sweet nectar drop, nature's lollipop!

26.description: Fuchsia hedges still glowing along western lanes, a constant companion to summer walks in Ireland
26.childFriendlyNote: The fuchsia hedges keep making new flowers all summer, each one dangling like a fairy lantern

26.description: Meadow brown butterflies abundant in grasslands and along hedgerows, lazy fluttering flight
26.childFriendlyNote: Brown butterflies with one eye-spot on each wing flutter lazily through the grass, like little pancakes with eyes!

26.description: Pufflings nearly fledged, almost as big as parents, getting ready for their first flight to the ocean
26.childFriendlyNote: The baby puffins are almost ready to leave! Soon they'll waddle to the cliff edge and jump into the sea!

26.description: Hogweed flowering along lanes and field edges, large flat white flower heads attracting beetles and hoverflies
26.childFriendlyNote: Big flat white flower plates attract all sorts of beetles and flies. It's like a bug restaurant!

26.description: Red clover at peak in meadows, bumblebees clinging to fuzzy pink flower heads
26.childFriendlyNote: Fat bumblebees cling to the pink clover balls. They're so heavy the whole flower nods down!

26.description: Common blues still widespread, first generation fading as second generation begins to emerge
26.childFriendlyNote: Some blue butterflies look fresh and bright and some look a bit tatty. The new ones are just born!

27.description: Fuchsia hedges at peak, magenta flowers everywhere in the west, berries starting to form on earliest blooms
27.childFriendlyNote: The fuchsia flowers are making dark purple berries. Did you know you can eat them? They taste a bit peppery!

27.description: Meadow browns abundant in every meadow and hedgerow margin, the commonest Irish summer butterfly
27.childFriendlyNote: Everywhere you walk in the grass, brown butterflies flutter up. Count how many you see in one minute!

27.description: Swifts still screaming over towns, chicks growing in nests under eaves, parents hunting insects at height
27.childFriendlyNote: The swifts are still screaming overhead. Their babies are hidden in nests under the roof!

27.description: Hogweed at peak, large platform flowers along every country lane, crawling with insects
27.childFriendlyNote: Look at how many different bugs are sitting on one hogweed flower. It's like a bug airport!

27.description: Bell heather starting to colour hillsides and bogs, deep purple-pink flowers on wiry stems
27.childFriendlyNote: The hillside is getting a purple tinge. Bell heather flowers are tiny and shaped like little bells!

27.description: Red squirrels active in conifer plantations and native woodlands, summer coat a bright ginger-red
27.childFriendlyNote: Bright ginger squirrels with tufty ears scamper through the trees. Ireland still has lots of red squirrels!

28.description: Fuchsia hedges still blooming magnificently, berries swelling on earliest flowers, bees visiting constantly
28.childFriendlyNote: Fuchsia hedges are still going strong. Watch the bees push inside the dangling flowers for nectar

28.description: Meadow browns at peak numbers, fluttering through every patch of long grass
28.childFriendlyNote: Walk through any long grass and brown butterflies flutter up around your knees, so many of them!

28.description: Ling heather and bell heather colouring hillsides and bogland, purple spreading across the landscape
28.childFriendlyNote: The hills are turning purple! The tiny heather flowers are opening by the thousand

28.description: Hogweed going over, flower heads turning brown and curling into seed heads, some still fresh
28.childFriendlyNote: The hogweed flowers are curling up like clenched fists. They're turning into seeds inside

28.description: Pufflings fledging from burrows, making their first journey to the sea under cover of darkness
28.childFriendlyNote: The baby puffins sneak out at night and run to the cliff. Then they jump into the dark sea! So brave!

28.description: Red squirrels busy in woodlands, young squirrels exploring independently for the first time
28.childFriendlyNote: Young red squirrels are out exploring on their own. They're a bit clumsy and very curious!

29.description: Heather spreading purple across hillsides and blanket bogs, bees buzzing in the warm summer air
29.childFriendlyNote: The hills are turning purple with heather. Listen to all the bees humming as they collect heather honey!

29.description: Fuchsia hedges still flowering, dark purple berries forming alongside fresh magenta blooms
29.childFriendlyNote: The fuchsia has flowers and berries at the same time. The berries are like tiny dark purple grapes

29.description: First blackberries starting to ripen in sheltered sunny spots, most still green or red
29.childFriendlyNote: The blackberries are starting! Look for the first black ones in the sunniest spots, but most are still red

29.description: Meadow browns still common but some looking worn, wings tattered at the edges
29.childFriendlyNote: Some meadow browns have tatty wings now. They've been flying all summer and it shows!

29.description: Swifts still screaming over towns but numbers starting to thin as earliest birds begin departure
29.childFriendlyNote: Some swifts are already heading back to Africa. Enjoy watching them while they're still here!

29.description: Red squirrels beginning to cache food for autumn, busy collecting hazelnuts and pine cones
29.childFriendlyNote: The red squirrels are being extra busy. They're hiding nuts everywhere for when winter comes!

30.description: Heather at peak, hillsides and bogs a blaze of purple, the air humming with bees making heather honey
30.childFriendlyNote: The purple hills are buzzing! Thousands of bees are making the most delicious dark heather honey

30.description: Blackberries ripening in hedgerows, first properly juicy dark fruits ready to pick on south-facing banks
30.childFriendlyNote: The first black ones are ready! Pick the darkest fattest berries and your fingers go purple

30.description: Fuchsia hedges still flowering along western lanes, berries ripening alongside new blooms
30.childFriendlyNote: The fuchsia keeps making flowers and berries together. It just doesn't know when to stop!

30.description: Swifts departing, screaming parties getting smaller over towns as birds head south to Africa
30.childFriendlyNote: The swifts are leaving! Wave goodbye. They won't land until they get all the way to Africa

30.description: Rowan berries turning orange, heavy clusters bending branches in hedgerows and mountainsides
30.childFriendlyNote: The rowan tree is covered in bunches of orange berries. Birds will go crazy for them soon!

30.description: Painted lady butterflies arriving from the continent in variable numbers, feeding on thistles and knapweed
30.childFriendlyNote: An orange and black butterfly flew here from Africa! It's a painted lady and she loves thistle flowers

31.description: Heather at peak on uplands and bogs, the characteristic purple August landscape of Ireland
31.childFriendlyNote: August is heather time! The hills are like a purple blanket spread across the land

31.description: Blackberries ripening fast in the summer heat, hedgerows heavy with dark juicy fruit
31.childFriendlyNote: Blackberry picking time! The fattest juiciest ones are at the top where nobody can reach, typical!

31.description: Rowan berries bright orange-red, heavy clusters drooping on branches, birds starting to feed
31.childFriendlyNote: The rowan berries are bright orange now. Blackbirds and thrushes are starting to feast!

31.description: Fuchsia hedges still flowering in the west, though peak is passing, berries abundant
31.childFriendlyNote: The fuchsia flowers are slowing down but the berries are getting bigger and darker

31.description: Meadow browns still flying but looking increasingly worn, late-season individuals still fresh
31.childFriendlyNote: The meadow browns are getting a bit ragged now. They've had a busy summer of flying!

31.description: Red squirrels busy collecting and caching hazelnuts, active in the canopy and on the ground
31.childFriendlyNote: The red squirrels are stuffing their cheeks with hazelnuts and burying them for winter. Will they remember where?

32.description: Heather still magnificent on hills and bogs, bees still busy making the last of the heather honey
32.childFriendlyNote: Purple heather still covers the hills. The bees are working hard to make one last batch of honey!

32.description: Blackberries at peak, every hedgerow dripping with ripe dark fruit, an August tradition
32.childFriendlyNote: It's the best time for blackberries! Grab a bucket and pick as many as you can. Watch out for thorns!

32.description: Rowan berries brilliant scarlet, birds feeding heavily, berries beginning to disappear
32.childFriendlyNote: The rowan berries are traffic-light red! Blackbirds are gobbling them up as fast as they can

32.description: Swallows still feeding young, second broods fledging, gathering in growing flocks on wires
32.childFriendlyNote: Baby swallows are sitting on the wires begging mum and dad for food. Their mouths are so wide open!

32.description: Red admiral butterflies feeding on bramble flowers and ripe blackberries, black wings with red bands
32.childFriendlyNote: A beautiful black butterfly with red stripes sits on the blackberries drinking the juice. It's a red admiral!

32.description: Ragwort in flower along roadsides and waste ground, visited by cinnabar moth caterpillars with yellow and black stripes
32.childFriendlyNote: Yellow ragwort flowers have amazing stripy caterpillars, black and gold like tiny tigers munching the leaves!

33.description: Heather past peak, purple fading to brown on the earliest flowers, still beautiful on sheltered slopes
33.childFriendlyNote: The heather is going brown in places but there's still purple on the sheltered slopes

33.description: Blackberries still abundant, later ripening berries on shaded branches, some going mouldy on warm days
33.childFriendlyNote: Still loads of blackberries. The ones hiding in the shade are just getting ripe now!

33.description: Swallows gathering on telephone wires in growing flocks, preparing for the long migration south
33.childFriendlyNote: The swallows are lining up on the wires like musical notes. They're planning their big trip to Africa!

33.description: Red admirals frequent in gardens, feeding on fallen fruit and late flowers, sunbathing on warm walls
33.childFriendlyNote: Red admirals love rotten apples. Look for them sitting on the ground with their wings spread open, sunbathing!

33.description: Rowan berries being stripped by birds, some trees already bare, mistle thrushes defending laden trees
33.childFriendlyNote: The birds have eaten most of the rowan berries already! One angry thrush guards the last ones

33.description: Red squirrels frantically caching hazelnuts and acorns for winter stores
33.childFriendlyNote: The red squirrels are so busy, running up and down burying nuts. They'll need them when it gets cold!

34.description: Blackberries still ripening but the season is waning, last good picking before they go seedy
34.childFriendlyNote: Last chance for blackberries! Old tradition says not to pick them after September. The devil spits on them!

34.description: Swallow flocks growing, staging along wires and over reed beds before the journey to Africa
34.childFriendlyNote: Hundreds of swallows sit on the wires chattering. They're getting ready for a 6000 mile flight!

34.description: Red admirals feeding up on fallen fruit and ivy flowers, storing energy for migration or overwintering
34.childFriendlyNote: Red admirals are eating as much as they can. Rotten plums are their favourite! They need energy for winter

34.description: Heather fading to russet brown, seed heads forming, the purple season drawing to a close
34.childFriendlyNote: The purple heather is going brown and rusty. It held its colour for most of August!

34.description: Elder berries ripening in hedgerows, heavy clusters turning from green to dark purple-black
34.childFriendlyNote: The elder tree's berries are going dark purple. Birds love them and people make them into cordial!

34.description: Horse chestnuts ripening, prickly green cases starting to split open, conkers just visible inside
34.childFriendlyNote: Look up at the horse chestnut. The prickly green balls are getting fat and starting to crack open!

35.description: Last blackberries fading, many going mouldy, an Irish tradition says they shouldn't be picked past the end of September
35.childFriendlyNote: The blackberries are going soft and mouldy now. The season is ending, but what a feast it was!

35.description: Swallows beginning to depart, large flocks still visible over lakes and reed beds in the evenings
35.childFriendlyNote: Some swallows have already left for Africa. Wave goodbye and wish them a safe flight!

35.description: Conkers starting to fall, prickly cases splitting to reveal glossy brown seeds
35.childFriendlyNote: The first conkers are falling! Crack open a prickly case and find the beautiful shiny brown treasure inside

35.description: Elder berries ripe and heavy, dark purple-black clusters drooping on red stems
35.childFriendlyNote: Elderberries are ripe and so dark they're almost black. Birds love them and they stain your fingers purple!

35.description: Ivy flower buds forming, the round green clusters about to open, vital late food for insects
35.childFriendlyNote: Little green balls are forming on the ivy. They'll open into flowers that feed bees and butterflies in autumn!

35.description: Red admirals still active, feeding on windfall fruit in gardens and warm sheltered spots
35.childFriendlyNote: Red admirals are sunbathing on warm walls. They spread their dark wings wide to soak up the last heat

36.description: Conkers falling in parks and playing fields, prickly cases cracking open on impact
36.childFriendlyNote: Conker season! Stamp on the prickly green shells to find the beautiful shiny brown conker inside

36.description: Last swallows departing Ireland, stragglers still swooping over fields and water
36.childFriendlyNote: The very last swallows are leaving. They'll fly all the way to South Africa! See you next spring!

36.description: Ivy flowers opening, pale green blooms buzzing with bees, wasps and hoverflies, a vital autumn nectar source
36.childFriendlyNote: The ivy is flowering and buzzing with bees! When other flowers are gone, ivy keeps the bees fed

36.description: First autumn fungi appearing: fly agaric, puffballs and field mushrooms popping up after rain
36.childFriendlyNote: Mushrooms are popping up overnight like magic! The red spotty ones are fly agaric, beautiful but don't touch!

36.description: Red squirrels in a frenzy of food caching, burying hazelnuts and acorns across the woodland floor
36.childFriendlyNote: The red squirrels are running around like crazy hiding food. They bury hundreds of nuts but forget where some are!

36.description: Elder berries fully ripe, birds stripping the clusters, stems left bare and red
36.childFriendlyNote: The birds have eaten most of the elderberries. Just the empty red stems are left dangling!

37.description: Conkers at peak, falling thickly in parks, kids collecting the shiniest specimens
37.childFriendlyNote: Conkers everywhere! The shiniest ones feel so smooth and cool in your hand. Who has the biggest?

37.description: Ivy flowers in full bloom, covered in feeding insects, the most important late-season nectar source in Ireland
37.childFriendlyNote: Ivy flowers smell sweet and sticky. Watch all the different insects having their autumn feast!

37.description: Fungi season building, bracket fungi on trees, fairy rings in grass, puffballs in meadows
37.childFriendlyNote: More mushrooms appearing every day. Look for fairy rings in the grass, perfect circles of toadstools!

37.description: Robins starting autumn territorial singing, the familiar thin sweet song returning after summer silence
37.childFriendlyNote: The robin is singing again after being quiet all summer! Its sweet thin song says "this is my garden!"

37.description: First hints of autumn colour in the canopy, birches turning yellow, wild cherry going orange-red
37.childFriendlyNote: The trees are starting to change. Some leaves are going yellow and gold like nature is painting them!

37.description: Red squirrels active from dawn, collecting the autumn nut harvest with urgency
37.childFriendlyNote: Red squirrels dash about stuffing acorns and hazelnuts into hiding spots. They forget about a quarter of them!

38.description: Autumn colour building in woodlands and hedgerows, beech going copper, oak turning brown, sycamore yellow
38.childFriendlyNote: The trees are on fire with colour, gold, orange, red, brown! How many different colours can you count?

38.description: Last conkers falling, leaves of horse chestnut already browning and curling
38.childFriendlyNote: The last conkers are falling. Get them quick before they lose their shine and go dull!

38.description: Fungi at peak, woodland floors dotted with many species: chanterelles, boletes, waxcaps in old grassland
38.childFriendlyNote: The woodland floor is a mushroom gallery, every shape, colour and size! Look but don't pick

38.description: Ivy flowers still going strong, one of the last nectar sources keeping bees and butterflies going
38.childFriendlyNote: The ivy flowers are the last restaurant open for bees. They're so grateful for the sweet nectar!

38.description: Robins in full autumn song, fighting for winter territories, their thin sweet tune carrying in the cool air
38.childFriendlyNote: Robins are singing so much now. Each one is saying "this bit of the garden is mine!"

38.description: First fieldfares arriving from Scandinavia, chattering flocks settling into hawthorn hedgerows
38.childFriendlyNote: New birds have arrived from the frozen north! Fieldfares come to Ireland for our mild winter, smart!

39.description: Peak autumn colour in many woodlands, though Atlantic gales may strip leaves early in exposed areas
39.childFriendlyNote: The trees are at their most colourful! But a big storm could blow the leaves off. Enjoy them quick!

39.description: Fungi peak continuing, fly agaric under birch trees, giant puffballs in meadows, waxcaps in old grassland
39.childFriendlyNote: Kick a giant puffball gently and watch the cloud of brown spores puff out like smoke. Each spore could grow a new one!

39.description: Fieldfare flocks building in hedgerows and fields, chattering as they strip hawthorn berries
39.childFriendlyNote: Noisy flocks of fieldfares are gobbling red hawthorn berries. They sound like they're arguing over the best ones!

39.description: Ivy flowers fading, small green berries beginning to form, still attracting late insects on warm days
39.childFriendlyNote: The ivy flowers are turning into tiny green berries. They'll go black later and feed the birds in winter

39.description: Robins conspicuous on bare branches, singing their winter song, following gardeners for worms
39.childFriendlyNote: The robin follows you when you dig the garden. It watches for worms and hops closer and closer!

39.description: Red squirrels making final caches before winter, fur thickening and ear tufts growing longer
39.childFriendlyNote: The red squirrels are getting their winter coats. Their ear tufts are growing longer and fluffier!

40.description: Autumn colour fading, many trees bare after Atlantic storms, oaks still holding their brown leaves
40.childFriendlyNote: The wind is shaking the coloured leaves off. Run through the falling leaves and try to catch one!

40.description: Fungi still abundant after autumn rain, bracket fungi on trees lasting all season, woodland floor dotted with toadstools
40.childFriendlyNote: New mushrooms pop up after every rain. Some look like shelves on trees, they're called bracket fungi!

40.description: Fieldfares widespread in hedgerows and farmland, large chattering flocks moving through the landscape
40.childFriendlyNote: Big flocks of fieldfares move noisily through the hedges. When the berries run out they'll hop into the fields

40.description: Robins very conspicuous on bare branches, red breast bright against the grey autumn sky
40.childFriendlyNote: With the leaves falling, the robin's red breast is easy to spot. It stands out like a little torch!

40.description: Starling flocks building, evening murmurations starting to form over reed beds and towns
40.childFriendlyNote: Hundreds of starlings swirl together at sunset like a living cloud. It's called a murmuration!

40.description: Holly berries turning red on female trees, the prickly dark green leaves standing out as other trees go bare
40.childFriendlyNote: Red holly berries are appearing! The prickly leaves protect them but birds still manage to eat them

41.description: Starling murmurations growing, thousands of birds creating spectacular aerial displays at dusk
41.childFriendlyNote: The starling cloud gets bigger every evening, they swirl and swoop together before going to sleep!

41.description: Late fungi still appearing, honey fungus glowing at tree bases, waxcaps in old grassland after rain
41.childFriendlyNote: Look for golden honey mushrooms at the bottom of trees. They grow in big bunches after the rain

41.description: Fieldfares feeding in fields and hedgerows, more birds still arriving from Scandinavia and Iceland
41.childFriendlyNote: More winter visitors are arriving. The fieldfares came from Iceland where it's already freezing cold!

41.description: Robins singing their thin sweet winter song, one of the few birds still in voice
41.childFriendlyNote: Most birds have stopped singing but the brave robin carries on. Its thin sweet song fills the quiet garden

41.description: Holly berries bright red, standing out against dark green leaves in bare hedgerows
41.childFriendlyNote: Red holly berries and dark prickly leaves look like Christmas decorations growing wild in the hedge!

41.description: Redwings arriving from Iceland and Scandinavia, feeding in hedgerows with fieldfares, cream eyestripe visible
41.childFriendlyNote: A new thrush with a cream stripe over its eye and red under its wing. Redwings come from the frozen north!

42.description: Starling murmurations spectacular, huge flocks creating living sculptures in the evening sky
42.childFriendlyNote: The starling show at sunset is amazing, thousands of birds flowing like a river in the sky!

42.description: Fieldfares settled into Irish hedgerows for winter, chattering flocks stripping berries systematically
42.childFriendlyNote: The fieldfares work through the hedge eating every berry, one bush at a time, like going down a buffet!

42.description: Redwings widespread now, feeding on berries by day, their thin "tseep" call heard overhead on clear nights as more arrive
42.childFriendlyNote: Go outside on a clear night and listen. You might hear thin "tseep" calls as redwings fly over in the dark!

42.description: Robins ever-present, singing from garden walls and bare branches, the soundtrack of Irish autumn
42.childFriendlyNote: The robin sits on the garden wall singing its gentle song. It's one of the friendliest birds in Ireland

42.description: Holly berries bright red, thrushes and blackbirds starting to feed on them in earnest
42.childFriendlyNote: The birds are starting to eat the holly berries. Will there be any left for Christmas decorations?

42.description: Wrens active in hedges and stone walls, tiny brown birds with an explosively loud song for their size
42.childFriendlyNote: The tiny wren is Ireland's favourite bird. It's smaller than your fist but sings so loud! Incredible!

43.description: Starling murmurations at peak, some of Ireland's best displays over Shannon and Lough Ennell
43.childFriendlyNote: The starling murmurations are the best show in Ireland, millions of birds dancing across the sky!

43.description: Wrens busy in stone walls and hedges, searching for spiders and insects, cocking their tiny tails
43.childFriendlyNote: Watch the tiny wren dart in and out of the stone wall. It holds its tail straight up like a little flag!

43.description: Redwings feeding in hedgerows and on playing fields, often with fieldfares, hopping through short grass
43.childFriendlyNote: Redwings and fieldfares feed together on the playing field. The redwings are smaller with a stripe over their eye

43.description: Robins bold and visible, following gardeners closely, singing from dawn to dusk
43.childFriendlyNote: The robin hops right up to you in the garden. It's hoping you'll turn over a leaf so it can grab a worm!

43.description: Late fungi still appearing after rain, velvet shank on dead wood, clouded funnel in leaf litter
43.childFriendlyNote: Even in late autumn, new mushrooms pop up after rain. They help the forest recycle dead leaves

43.description: Holly berries still red and shining, an important food source as other berries run out
43.childFriendlyNote: Holly berries glow red in the bare hedge. They're a lifeline for hungry birds when everything else is eaten

44.description: Starling murmurations still spectacular as days shorten, swirling clouds against orange sunset skies
44.childFriendlyNote: The starlings dance in the sunset sky. They make shapes like waves, tornadoes and giant whales!

44.description: Wrens looking for warm roost sites as nights get cold, sometimes huddling together in nest boxes
44.childFriendlyNote: On cold nights, wrens cuddle together for warmth. Once 63 wrens were found in one nest box!

44.description: Fieldfares in fields and hedgerows, moving to open ground when hedgerow berries run out
44.childFriendlyNote: The fieldfares have eaten all the hedge berries so now they're hunting for worms in the fields!

44.description: Robins singing from fence posts and bare branches, their sweet warble one of the few bird songs now
44.childFriendlyNote: In the quiet of late autumn, the robin's song sounds even more beautiful, like a tiny jewel of sound

44.description: Holly berries and leaves prominent as other plants die back, ready for traditional Christmas gathering
44.childFriendlyNote: Holly is one of the only green things left! Red berries and prickly leaves, getting ready for Christmas

44.description: Redwings widespread, feeding on berries and worms, their thin calls heard on still autumn nights
44.childFriendlyNote: Redwings hop across the grass turning over leaves. Flash! You see the orange-red under their wings

45.description: Starling murmurations continuing through November, flocks roosting in reeds, under bridges and in trees
45.childFriendlyNote: The starling dance goes on! At sunset, find a murmuration and watch the sky come alive

45.description: Wrens flitting through hedges and stone walls, Ireland's most loved small bird, the subject of Wren Day on St Stephen's
45.childFriendlyNote: The tiny wren is Ireland's favourite bird. On St Stephen's Day people dress up and go 'hunting the wren'!

45.description: Robins conspicuous in bare gardens, the Christmas robin of cards and stories
45.childFriendlyNote: The robin on the Christmas card is real! It sits in your garden singing even when it's cold and grey

45.description: Fieldfares feeding in fields and pastures, often with redwings, moving to new areas when food runs out
45.childFriendlyNote: Fieldfares and redwings travel together like best friends: safety in numbers when a hawk flies over!

45.description: Most deciduous trees now bare, their beautiful branching patterns visible against grey Irish skies
45.childFriendlyNote: With no leaves, you can see every branch and twig. Each tree has its own special shape like a fingerprint!

45.description: A few gorse flowers still showing on sheltered bushes, proving the saying that gorse is never out of bloom
45.childFriendlyNote: Even in November, a few brave gorse flowers are shining yellow. This plant just never gives up!

46.description: Starling murmurations at their most dramatic as flocks reach maximum size in mid-November
46.childFriendlyNote: The starling murmurations are at their biggest now. Like a living fireworks display every sunset!

46.description: Wrens searching stone walls for spiders and insects, their explosive trill still ringing out on fine mornings
46.childFriendlyNote: The wren is so loud for such a tiny bird. Its song rattles like a tiny machine gun from the wall!

46.description: Robins singing from every garden and hedgerow, their winter song carrying in the still air
46.childFriendlyNote: The robin is the voice of the Irish winter, sweet and gentle when everything else is quiet

46.description: Redwings feeding across Ireland, visiting gardens in cold snaps, showing the flash of red under wings
46.childFriendlyNote: When it's really cold, redwings come into gardens to eat berries. Look for the red patch under their wings!

46.description: Holly berries glowing red in bare hedgerows, mistle thrushes fiercely defending their favourite trees
46.childFriendlyNote: One angry thrush guards the holly tree and chases away every other bird. Those berries are mine!

46.description: Grey herons standing motionless by ponds and streams, easier to spot now vegetation has died back
46.childFriendlyNote: A tall grey bird stands like a statue by the water, waiting... waiting... then stab! It grabs a fish!

47.description: Starling murmurations still stunning, the birds gathering from miles around before dropping into their roost
47.childFriendlyNote: Watch how the starlings all turn at exactly the same moment. No one bird is the leader!

47.description: Wrens huddling in sheltered spots on cold nights, sometimes dozens roosting together for warmth
47.childFriendlyNote: Wrens have sleepovers! They squeeze together in a nest box or hole to share body heat on cold nights

47.description: Robins singing bravely through the shortening days, one of the last birds singing at dusk
47.childFriendlyNote: Even as it gets dark so early, the robin keeps singing, a little melody to end the short November day

47.description: Fieldfares roaming farmland in noisy flocks, feeding on the last berries and on earthworms
47.childFriendlyNote: The fieldfares are chattering loudly as they search for food. They sound like they're having an argument!

47.description: Grey herons fishing at ponds and rivers, their patient hunting style easier to watch now bankside plants have died back
47.childFriendlyNote: Can you stand as still as a heron? It waits without moving for ages, then, splash! It catches a fish!

47.description: Holly berries bright red, a vital winter food for thrushes and blackbirds
47.childFriendlyNote: The holly berries are so red they glow in the grey November light. Birds depend on them for winter food

48.description: Starling murmurations continuing in late November, flocks twisting and turning in the gloaming
48.childFriendlyNote: The starlings are still putting on their evening show. They make shapes like giant animals in the sky!

48.description: Robins singing from bare branches and garden walls, very tame and confiding near humans
48.childFriendlyNote: The robin comes so close now. It's not shy at all! It knows you might turn over a stone and find it a snack

48.description: Wrens busy in walls and hedges, their loud trill a burst of energy on frosty mornings
48.childFriendlyNote: On a frosty morning the tiny wren lets out a trill so loud it makes you jump. What a voice for such a small bird!

48.description: Grey herons visible at ponds and along rivers, standing still as statues in the winter landscape
48.childFriendlyNote: The heron stands in the cold water without moving a feather. Patience is its superpower!

48.description: Holly berries being gathered for Christmas wreaths, thrushes competing with humans for the red fruits
48.childFriendlyNote: Time to gather holly for decorations! Be careful of the prickly leaves, ouch!

48.description: Redwings feeding in gardens during cold spells, stripping holly and cotoneaster berries
48.childFriendlyNote: When it's freezing cold, redwings come into gardens to eat berries. They must be really hungry!

49.description: Starling murmurations in early December, darkening skies filled with swirling flocks before roosting
49.childFriendlyNote: December evenings are perfect for starling watching. Wrap up warm and enjoy the sky ballet!

49.description: Robins singing their winter song, appearing on Christmas cards and in festive traditions
49.childFriendlyNote: The robin on the Christmas card is singing outside your window right now. Can you hear it?

49.description: Wrens active in hedges and walls, preparing for the old tradition of Wren Day on December 26th
49.childFriendlyNote: The wren is getting ready for its special day! On St Stephen's Day people dress up to celebrate the wren

49.description: Fieldfares in fields and hedgerows, feeding on whatever berries remain and on invertebrates in grassland
49.childFriendlyNote: The fieldfares are still here from the north. They'll stay all winter keeping warm in our mild Irish weather

49.description: Holly central to Christmas preparations, red berries and evergreen leaves a symbol of the season
49.childFriendlyNote: Holly is the star of Christmas decorations, red berries and shiny green leaves that stay on all winter!

49.description: Grey herons fishing at ponds, their hunched silhouette a familiar part of the winter waterside scene
49.childFriendlyNote: The heron hunches its shoulders against the cold like a grumpy old man, but it's actually a brilliant fisher!

50.description: Starling murmurations in the short December days, dramatic against the winter sunset
50.childFriendlyNote: The sun sets so early now. That means the starling show starts early too! Watch from your window

50.description: Robins at their most visible and confiding, hopping close to humans in gardens and parks
50.childFriendlyNote: The robin is your garden friend. It sits so close you could almost touch it! (But don't, let it come to you)

50.description: Wrens roosting communally in cold spells, searching stone walls and ivy for invertebrates by day
50.childFriendlyNote: The wren sneaks through the thickest brambles and ivy. It's so small it can fit through gaps you can't even see!

50.description: Foxes becoming more vocal as the mating season approaches, barking calls heard at night
50.childFriendlyNote: Was that a bark in the night? The foxes are starting to call to each other as winter gets deep

50.description: Fieldfares scattered across farmland and playing fields, chattering flocks a constant winter presence
50.childFriendlyNote: Fieldfares chatter away on the playing fields. They came all the way from the frozen north for our mild winter!

50.description: Ivy berries ripening, green clusters turning dark, a vital winter food for wood pigeons and blackbirds
50.childFriendlyNote: The ivy berries are going dark. Pigeons and blackbirds love them when everything else has been eaten

51.description: Robins prominent in the Christmas week landscape, singing from fence posts and bare holly branches
51.childFriendlyNote: It's Christmas week and the robin is singing! The real Christmas robin right there in your garden

51.description: Wrens active in hedges and walls. Wren Day (Lá an Dreoilín) on St Stephen's Day, December 26th, is an Irish tradition
51.childFriendlyNote: Tomorrow is Wren Day! People dress up as Wren Boys and go door to door. The wren is the King of All Birds!

51.description: Starling murmurations in the Christmas twilight, thousands of birds swirling before dropping to roost
51.childFriendlyNote: After Christmas dinner, go watch the starlings dance in the sky, nature's own light show!

51.description: Holly the centrepiece of Christmas decorations, brought indoors in the old Irish tradition
51.childFriendlyNote: Holly on the door, holly on the mantelpiece. Its red berries and green leaves mean Christmas is here!

51.description: Fox mating season beginning, bark-like screams echoing through cold night air in town and countryside
51.childFriendlyNote: Was that a scream outside on Christmas night? It's a fox calling. Their noisy time of year is starting!

51.description: In the mildest coastal areas, the very first snowdrop tips may be pushing through, a promise of spring to come
51.childFriendlyNote: In the warmest spots near the coast, tiny green snowdrop tips might already be poking up. Spring is coming!

52.description: Robins singing through the last days of the year, their sweet song a bridge between old year and new
52.childFriendlyNote: The robin sings goodbye to the old year and hello to the new one. Its song never stops, even in winter!

52.description: Wrens sheltering in stone walls and ivy on the coldest nights, tiny bodies burning through energy fast
52.childFriendlyNote: The tiny wren weighs about the same as a euro coin but survives the coldest nights! What a little hero!

52.description: Starling murmurations continuing through the year's end, a breathtaking display in the winter dusk
52.childFriendlyNote: The starlings are putting on their New Year show! Thousands of birds painting pictures in the sky

52.description: Fox mating season underway, eerie screaming calls echoing through the long winter nights
52.childFriendlyNote: The foxes are screaming in the dark. It sounds spooky but they're just talking to each other!

52.description: Fieldfares and redwings feeding across farmland, making the most of Ireland's mild oceanic winter
52.childFriendlyNote: The winter visitors from the north are settled in. Ireland's mild weather keeps them happy till spring!

52.description: A few gorse flowers visible on sheltered bushes even in late December, the eternal golden bloom of Ireland
52.childFriendlyNote: Even on the last day of the year, gorse has a few yellow flowers. It really never stops blooming!
